I'll build the threat model based on the review context.

The core issue: the server trusts a client-supplied `"purchased": true` flag to unlock premium, rather than validating the receipt server-side with the app store.

```json
  "schema": "threatline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-04",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["Mobile app", "Premium unlock endpoint", "Account/entitlement store"],
    "dataStores": ["Account/entitlement store"],
    "externalServices": ["App store (receipt issuer, not validated by server)"],
    "trustBoundaries": ["Mobile client <-> Server API"],
    "dataClasses": ["payment"],
    "exposure": "internal",
    "llmFeatures": false
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "Client can grant itself premium by sending purchased:true without paying",
      "scenario": "An attacker intercepts or replays the POST /premium/unlock request (e.g. via a proxy like Burp, a modified APK, or a crafted HTTP call) and simply sets \"purchased\": true without ever completing a real purchase. Since the server trusts this flag instead of validating the receipt, the attacker gets premium for free.",
      "component": "Premium unlock endpoint",
      "likelihood": 5,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "The server trusts the client flag \"purchased\": true and unlocks premium for the account." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V1.2.2", "V4.1.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-602"],
      "plainLanguage": "Anyone can fake the 'I paid' flag from their phone and get premium for free, no receipt check needed.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Server must validate purchase with the app store before unlocking premium",
        "given": "A client calls POST /premium/unlock with a receipt",
        "when": "The server processes the request",
        "then": "The server verifies the receipt directly with Apple/Google server-to-server and only unlocks premium if that verification succeeds, ignoring any client-supplied purchased flag"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Repudiation",
      "title": "No server-side proof a real purchase occurred, so fraud can't be detected or reversed",
      "scenario": "Because the endpoint accepts the client's say-so instead of an app-store-verified receipt, there is no record tying the unlock to an actual payment. Support/finance cannot distinguish legitimate purchases from exploited unlocks, and cannot revoke access when a receipt is later found to be refunded or invalid.",
      "component": "Premium unlock endpoint",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "When a purchase succeeds the app calls POST /premium/unlock with the receipt." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V1.2.2"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-345"],
      "plainLanguage": "Since the app doesn't actually check the receipt, there's no reliable way to prove who really paid or claw back access on refunds.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Store verified receipt data, not just a boolean",
        "given": "A purchase unlock request is received",
        "when": "The server validates the receipt",
        "then": "The server stores the app-store transaction ID and validation result so refunds/chargebacks can later revoke premium"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "No server-side check that the receipt belongs to the calling account",
      "scenario": "Even if receipt validation is added later, if the design doesn't bind the receipt to the authenticated account, an attacker could reuse one valid receipt (their own, a leaked one, or a refunded one shared online) across many accounts to unlock premium for free on all of them.",
      "component": "Premium unlock endpoint",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "POST /premium/unlock with the receipt" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V4.1.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-639"],
      "plainLanguage": "A single valid purchase receipt could be shared or reused to unlock premium on many different accounts.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Bind each receipt to one account, once",
        "given": "A receipt is validated as genuine",
        "when": "It is applied to unlock premium",
        "then": "The server records the receipt/transaction ID as consumed and rejects reuse on any other account"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Using the Threatline Security Reviewer role to analyze EVAL-04.

The core issue: the server trusts a client-supplied boolean flag to grant premium access instead of validating the purchase with the receipt against the payment provider.

```json
{
  "schema": "threatline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-04",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["Mobile app", "POST /premium/unlock endpoint", "Account premium flag"],
    "dataStores": ["Account/premium status store"],
    "externalServices": ["App store / IAP receipt validation service (implied, not called)"],
    "trustBoundaries": ["Mobile client to backend API"],
    "dataClasses": [],
    "exposure": "internal",
    "llmFeatures": false
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "Server trusts client-sent 'purchased' flag to unlock premium",
      "scenario": "An attacker intercepts or crafts the POST /premium/unlock request and sets \"purchased\": true without ever completing a real purchase. Since the server does not verify the receipt with the app store, premium is unlocked for free.",
      "component": "POST /premium/unlock endpoint",
      "likelihood": 5,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "The server trusts the client flag \"purchased\": true and unlocks premium for the account." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V1.2.4", "V4.1.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-602"],
      "plainLanguage": "Anyone can fake the 'I paid' message from the app and get premium for free, because the server just believes the app's word for it.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Validate purchase receipt server-side before granting premium",
        "given": "A client calls POST /premium/unlock",
        "when": "The server receives a purchase receipt",
        "then": "The server must independently verify the receipt with the app store / payment provider's verification API and only unlock premium if that verification succeeds, ignoring any client-supplied 'purchased' boolean"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "Replay of a valid receipt to unlock premium on other accounts",
      "scenario": "Because the endpoint relies on a receipt without confirming it hasn't been used before or binding it to the purchasing account, an attacker who obtains a valid receipt (their own, a leaked one, or shared screenshot) can replay it against multiple accounts to unlock premium repeatedly.",
      "component": "POST /premium/unlock endpoint",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "When a purchase succeeds the app calls POST /premium/unlock with the receipt." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V4.1.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-294"],
      "plainLanguage": "The same purchase proof could be reused on several accounts if the server doesn't check that it was already redeemed.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Bind receipts to a single account and prevent reuse",
        "given": "A receipt is submitted to unlock premium",
        "when": "The server validates the receipt",
        "then": "The server must check the receipt has not already been redeemed and that it is tied to the requesting account's purchase, rejecting duplicate or mismatched claims"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Repudiation",
      "title": "No link between validated purchase and account prevents dispute resolution",
      "scenario": "If the unlock endpoint only flips a flag based on client input with no stored, verified record of the actual transaction, the business cannot later prove or disprove whether a specific account's premium status came from a real purchase, complicating refunds, chargebacks, or abuse investigations.",
      "component": "Account premium flag",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "The server trusts the client flag \"purchased\": true and unlocks premium for the account." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V7.3.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-778"],
      "plainLanguage": "Without a real record of the verified purchase, support/finance can't tell later whether an account's premium was actually paid for.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Record verified purchase details, not just a boolean",
        "given": "A purchase is verified and premium is granted",
        "when": "The system records the grant",
        "then": "The system must store the verified receipt/transaction identifier and provider verification result against the account for later audit"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```
